title: Get a rover out from under a collapsed slab without bringing it down
instruction: Get the rover out from under the rubble onto the pad.
context: In a collapse, rescuers read which piece carries which before moving anything, and take a load before removing what holds it. Here a concrete slab bridges over a stranded 14 kg rover, 1.3 cm above its roof, on a block and on a smooth steel pipe lying on a steep debris face. A fallen timber lies across the rover's way out, the obvious thing to clear, but its far end is wedged against the pipe, and while the slab bears on the pipe the timber is jammed: it cannot be lifted, and the rover runs into it. The slab's end has to be held (a bar stands out of it) to take its load off, then the timber lifted away and the rover drawn out; the pipe rolls to a lip and the slab settles 8 mm. Unlike #1148 (a crib swapped under a loaded beam), #1147/#1281 (a panel freed from a leaning rack in order), #952 (the crib that holds a hatch) or #1310 (a load braced while the sheet under it is pulled), here the piece in the way carries nothing itself: it holds the prop that does, and nothing marks it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Track: an earth-brown sheet of painted PVC foil 0.6 mm thick, taped to the table from x 10 to 42, y -30 to 56, with a white tape line (6 mm) across it at y 22 (the pad beyond it). Slab: precast concrete 32 x 16 x 1.2 cm (1.5 kg), centred over (26, 0), its underside 13 cm up, with a rusted steel bar 1 x 3 x 3 cm standing out of its top at (36, 0). Under its near end a concrete block 4 x 8 x 13 cm at (14, 0). Under its far end a steel pipe 10 cm across and 28 cm long (1.0 kg, thin wall), its axis along y from y -5 to 23, centred at x 41.5; it lies on a smooth steel plate on a debris face falling toward the rover at 40 degrees, with a fixed lip of broken block 2 cm short of the pipe on that side (x 34.5, from y -5 to 18). A fallen timber 24 x 4 x 6 cm (0.34 kg) lies along x at y 21.5, from x 14 to 38: its near end against a fixed rock (x 10 to 14), its far end against the pipe. Rover: a rover built for the rig at the size of a 1:18 trail crawler (Traxxas TRX-4M body shell in polycarbonate, painted yellow with a white roof), 26.2 x 12.4 x 11.7 cm, on an aluminium chassis with steel axles and about 13 kg of lead (1.15 L) cast to fill the body between and over the axles: 14 kg in all, centre of mass 5.5 cm up; hard rubber tyres 5.6 cm across, the front pair crowned (rounded tread), the rear flat; the front axle a turntable pivoting at its middle (both front wheels turn together); driveshafts removed so its wheels roll freely; steering servo unpowered, so the front wheels stay where they are put; its origin (midway between the axles) at (26, 0), heading +y (toward the robot's left), front wheels straight. Tow tabs: dark grey 3D-printed PLA tabs 5.0 x 1.6 x 1.6 cm on the middle of each bumper, 4.5 cm up, each with a post 1 cm across and 3 cm tall at its tip. Steering tiller: a red pin 1 cm across, top 11.2 cm up.
scoring: 0 if at any time, while the rover is under the slab (any point of its rear treads short of the slab's edge at y 8 cm), the slab comes more than 1 cm closer to the rover than where the scene put them (its nearest point to the rover's body, 13 mm at the start), held or not; or, once the rover is out, more than 1 cm below its reference while no gripper holds its bar (the reference: where the slab was at the last step at which a gripper held its bar with the rover out; where the scene put it if there was none) (the point between the pad tips within 2.5 cm of the bar's middle and the fingers shut on it, under 1.5 cm apart); or any piece of the pile (slab, pipe, block, timber) comes within 2 mm of the rover's body. Otherwise, at the end, after 2 s with the rover at rest (under 5 mm/s and 0.05 rad/s) and released (no point of either gripper, and no point along either arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the rover, its wheels and steering; no gripper holding the slab's bar): 1.0 all four tyres on the pad (every point of each tread past y 22 cm, inside the track, the lowest point within 5 mm of it); 0.5 the rover out from under the slab (every point of both rear treads past y 8 cm); 0 otherwise. A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Rebuild the pile on its marks: block, pipe on its plate against nothing, slab, then the timber between the fixed rock and the pipe; the rover under it.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The pipe's friction on its plate and on the slab is 0.25 (smooth steel): a round prop pinched under a load holds by friction while tan(slope/2) is below its friction, so a rough prop would stay without the timber; the steep face and smooth pipe make it roll. Probe: with the timber gone the slab comes down 15.6 mm (3 of 3). Real build: both pipe contacts need friction under tan 20 deg = 0.36 (smooth or greased steel).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (one arm went to the rover's rear and stayed there; nothing was moved); demo: 1.0
